:::{#exm-indpt-auto}
#### Origin and cylinder count in the Auto data

In the Auto data of [the random experiment](probability-basics.qmd#exm-random-experiment),
pick a car model [at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice),
and let $X_1$ indicate that it is American
(`origin == 1` in the data)
and $X_2$ indicate that it has four cylinders.
By @thm-indpt-pmf,
$X_1 \ind X_2$
[if and only if](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-iff)
the [joint PMF](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-pmf) factors:
$\P(X_1 = x_1, X_2 = x_2) = \P(X_1 = x_1)\,\P(X_2 = x_2)$
for every pair of values $(x_1, x_2)$.
Here are the two sides of that equation for the pair of values $(1, 1)$,
with the factors on the right being [marginal](random-variables.qmd#def-marginal)
[PMFs](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf):

```{r}
#| label: exm-indpt-auto-pmf
auto <- readr::read_csv("data/auto.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
is_american <- auto$origin == 1
has_four <- auto$cylinders == 4
p_joint <- mean(is_american & has_four)
p_american <- mean(is_american)
p_four <- mean(has_four)
c(left_side = p_joint, right_side = p_american * p_four)
```

The left side, the [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability)
of an American car with four cylinders, is
`{r} round(p_joint, 3)`,
but the right side is
`{r} round(p_american * p_four, 3)`.
The factorization fails at $(1, 1)$,
so $X_1$ and $X_2$ are not [independent](#def-indpt):
learning that a car is American changes the probability that it has four cylinders
(@fig-indpt-auto).

```{r}
#| label: exm-indpt-auto-alt
#| echo: false
fig_alt_indpt <- paste(
  "Bar chart of the fraction of car models with four cylinders.",
  "The bar for American cars is far below the bar for non-American cars,",
  "and the dashed line for all cars lies between them."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-indpt-auto
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   The fraction of car models with four cylinders,
#|   among American and non-American cars.
#|   The dashed line is the fraction among all cars,
#|   which both bars would match if $X_1$ and $X_2$ were independent.
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt_indpt
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
by_origin <- auto |>
  dplyr::mutate(american = origin == 1, four = cylinders == 4) |>
  dplyr::summarise(fraction_four = mean(four), .by = american)
indpt_plot <- by_origin |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = american, y = fraction_four) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#1f77b4") +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = p_four, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "American", y = "Fraction with four cylinders")
qnp::interactive_plot(plot = indpt_plot, alt = fig_alt_indpt)
```
:::
